title: 2019 Hurlstone Legal Studies Trial
notes: The PDF contains no multiple-choice answer key; answers are reasoned and require checking against any published trial solutions.

questions.stem: Which of the following are types of criminal penalties used in NSW?

options.B: No conviction recorded, suspended sentence, weekend detention
options.C: Forfeiture of assets, community service order, capital punishment
options.D: Criminal infringement notice, diversionary programs, home detention

questions.answerNote: B and D are both plausible: B (no conviction recorded, suspended sentence, weekend detention) and D (criminal infringement notice, home detention) both include options since abolished or not strictly penalties; A and C are wrong (corporal/capital punishment). B kept as the closer match to sentencing options.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a civil and political right?
questions.answerNote: Freedom of religion is a civil and political right; Education and health care are social rights.

questions.stem: A magistrate or judge has the power to make a decision based on the particular circumstances of a case within a set range of possibilities. What is this power known as?
questions.answerNote: Judicial discretion is a decision within the range permitted by law.

questions.stem: Which court is the final court of appeal for criminal offences?
questions.answerNote: The High Court is Australia’s final appellate court.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a mitigating factor in a sentencing decision?

options.A: The offender abused a position of trust in relation to the victim
options.B: The offence was committed for financial gain

questions.answerNote: A guilty plea is mitigating; The other listed circumstances aggravate the offence.

questions.stem: Helen was charged with murder. Her defence of diminished responsibility was accepted by the court and Helen was found guilty of manslaughter. For Helen’s defence to be accepted by the court it was necessary for her to show evidence that she

options.C: Suffers from a mental abnormality that caused her to commit the crime

questions.answerNote: Diminished responsibility requires a mental abnormality substantially impairing responsibility.

questions.stem: Which of the following human rights is directly recognised in the Australian Constitution?
questions.answerNote: The Constitution expressly protects voting rights in limited circumstances; The other options are not express guarantees.

questions.stem: In the strict liability offence of selling alcohol to a 16 year old, which of the following must be proven?
questions.answerNote: Strict liability removes the need to prove mens rea but still requires proof of the prohibited act.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a widely recognised element of human rights?
questions.answerNote: Inalienability is a widely recognised characteristic of human rights.

questions.stem: The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights is an example of which of the following?
questions.answerNote: The ICCPR is a multilateral treaty.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an alternative to traditional sentencing methods and involves bringing together the offender and the victim?
questions.answerNote: Restorative justice is the general approach of bringing offender and victim together; Circle Sentencing (C) is plausible but centres on the Aboriginal community and elders.

questions.stem: The transportation or the illegal entry of a person across an international border is best known as which type of international crime?
questions.answerNote: Cross-border transportation or entry is characteristic of transnational crime.

questions.stem: Tony and friends are blocking a public pathway and refuse a reasonable police direction to move on. What type of offence is this?
questions.answerNote: Obstructing a public pathway and disobeying a move-on direction are public order matters.

questions.stem: The forcible removal of a person from one country and returning them to their country of origin is referred to as which of the following?
questions.answerNote: Removal of a non-citizen from a country is deportation.

questions.stem: Joseph is 15 years old and is found guilty of assault. The Children’s Court decides that he serve 12 months in a Juvenile Justice Centre. What is this an example of?
questions.answerNote: A Children’s Court detention order is a control order.

questions.stem: Nicolas is homeless and shoplifted some food to eat. What is likely to be the main factor leading to his criminal behaviour?
questions.answerNote: Changed from B. Homelessness and poverty point to economic factors as the main cause; Necessity (B) is a plausible alternative but is a defence rather than a causal factor.

questions.stem: The police in Wagga attempt to address the high levels of juvenile crime through establishing employment training programs at the local Youth and Community Centre. This is an example of which of the following?
questions.answerNote: Employment training addresses social risk factors linked to juvenile offending.

questions.stem: The 2006 Jury Amendments (Verdict) Act (NSW) allowed for majority verdicts in NSW trials. Under which of the following circumstances would majority verdicts be permissible?

options.A: When 9 out of 12 jurors agree on a verdict
options.B: Where there is a hung jury
options.C: Where reasonable time for deliberation has occurred and the court is satisfied a unanimous verdict can’t be reached

questions.answerNote: A majority verdict requires sufficient deliberation and a court direction when unanimity is unlikely.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a post sentencing option in NSW?
questions.answerNote: Sex offender registration can apply after sentencing.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a non-legal measure that addresses human rights issues?

options.A: Decisions by the Australian Human Rights Commission
options.C: Decisions by the Administrative Appeals Tribunal
options.D: Published reports in the Australian media

questions.answerNote: Media reporting is a non-legal measure that can expose and generate pressure about rights issues.
